course_name_original: MACCHINE E AZIONAMENTI ELETTRICI E COMPLEMENTI (DG0256)
course_name_en: ELECTRIC MACHINES AND DRIVES AND COMPLEMENTS (DG0256)
prerequisites: Skills in electrotechnics: analysis of circuits in sinusoidal steady state, with particular reference to the use of symbolic calculation and three-phase systems; principles of electromagnetism.

learning_outcomes.text: The student acquires theoretical and applicative knowledge on the main direct current and alternating current electric motors and variable speed drives.
The student will be able to choose and analyze the operation of electric motors and drives for civil and industrial applications.
The course aims to provide theoretical and applicative knowledge on single-phase and three-phase transformers used in electricity generation, transmission, distribution, and utilization plants.
The student will have knowledge and understanding of the theory and control of the main electric motors and drives.
The student will know how to understand and explain the physical mechanisms of the main electric motors and drives.
The student will know how to understand the principles of electric motor speed control.
The student will have the ability to choose electric motors and drives based on applications.
The student will have the ability to read and understand texts related to correlated topics.
The student will have acquired knowledge of the transformer models, preparatory for subsequent courses.
The student will have acquired the ability to determine the steady-state operating characteristics using mathematical models and equivalent circuits.

syllabus_topics: Models of electric motors in permanent regime: direct current motors, asynchronous motors.
Models of electric motors in any variable regime: direct current motors, asynchronous motors, synchronous motors.
Speed control of direct current motors in operating quadrants.
Independently excited motors: armature voltage control, armature current control, excitation voltage control.
Speed control of asynchronous motors: variable frequency and constant flux control, reduced flux control.
Vectorial speed control of asynchronous motors.
Vectorial speed control for permanent magnet and reluctance synchronous motors.
Direct current converters: bridge converters and choppers.
Variable speed direct current drives: single and multi-quadrant drives.
Alternating current converters: 6-step and PWM inverters, modulation techniques, current control.
Variable speed alternating current drives: voltage/frequency control, vectorial control.
Operation of alternating current motors fed with distorted voltage.
Fundamentals of electromagnetism: linear and non-linear magnetic circuits; permanent magnets.

THE SINGLE-PHASE TRANSFORMER: Generalities and constructive notes; model and equivalent network: the ideal and real transformer, the real transformer in sinusoidal regime; simplified equivalent networks; experimental tests and determination of transformer parameters; loaded operation: voltage drops and efficiency; transformers in parallel.

THE THREE-PHASE TRANSFORMER: Core structure; fundamental phase connections; transformation ratio, hourly index and groups; homopolar impedance; equivalent networks; star point potential displacement; star point potential rotation; determination of equivalent network parameters.

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam (3 questions on main course content) for Electric Machines and Drives
Oral exam (1 question on main course content) for Complements of Electric Machines and Drives

assessment_rules: The oral exam for Electric Machines and Drives, consisting of 3 questions, aims to ascertain knowledge of speed control principles, theory and control of electric motors and drives, and the ability to analyze the electric drive system, choose motors and drives for applications, and understand related texts. The oral exam for Complements of Electric Machines and Drives, consisting of one question, aims to ascertain knowledge and understanding of physical phenomena and operating principles of single-phase and three-phase transformers, ability to model phenomena with mathematical models and equivalent circuits, ability to determine steady-state operating characteristics, and knowledge of transformer application fields. The overall evaluation is a final grade.
